reports.title: Stephen Verrall: Prevention of future deaths report

concerns.quote: I was informed that CQC did not routinely check window restrictors on inspections
I heard that Stephen had managed to leave the home unaccompanied on several occasions

reports.title: Terrence Taylor: Prevention of future deaths report

concerns.quote: The current standards have been developed to prevent accidental falling from windows. They do not deal with deliberate attempts to defeat the restrictor, which may well be the situation encountered residential care homes, as in fact occurred in this case. This limitation is not known or understood by operators of residential care homes.
concerns.hazard: window restrictors ineffective against deliberate defeat

concerns.quote: window restrictors tested to current British Standards may be inadequate in preventing a determined effort to force a window open beyond 100mm
concerns.hazard: window restrictors ineffective against deliberate defeat

concerns.quote: it is suggested that window restrictors (and their fixings) are capable of withstanding push forces of at least 850N

Operators of care homes are likely to consider they are taking reasonable steps to secure windows by fitting restrictors that meet the British Standards, whereas the 2013 Department of Health Guidance and the 2019 Health and Safety Executive research indicates that is not so

Action is required to ensure operators of care homes are provided with reliable, up to date guidance and to ensure that the limitations of the British Standard are widely known and understood by operators of residential care homes

Action is required to review the British Standard relating to window restrictors to consider whether some different standard or qualification to the existing standard is required in respect of residential care homes and/or deliberate acts to disable window restrictors

links.explanation: Both reports concern the adequacy of window restrictors in care settings to prevent residents from falling or exiting unsafely. The earlier report highlights a lack of routine checks by the regulator, while the later report points out that existing standards may be insufficient and calls for stronger restrictors and better guidance.
